title: Content Architecture
brief: A commercial, agent-ready Sanity CMS starter kit in Next.js 16 and Astro 7 editions: a page-builder CMS with in-app Studio, visual editing, draft mode, SEO helpers, a seed dataset, and Plop scaffolding. Its differentiator is agentic-coding workflow support — it ships AGENTS.md plus scoped skills, two preconfigured MCP servers (one reads the running dev server, one drives real Chrome for screenshots/traces), an editable llms.txt, and token-light Markdown versions of every page served to agents via content negotiation. One license per buyer covers unlimited personal, commercial, and client projects; it is a paid product, not open source.
details: Content Architecture (contentarchitecture.dev) is a commercial, agent-ready starter kit for building content sites with Sanity CMS, sold in two editions sharing one architecture: Next.js 16.3 with the App Router and React Compiler, or Astro 7, both on Sanity v6, strict TypeScript, Tailwind 4, and Biome. It ships an in-app Sanity Studio mounted at /studio, a catch-all pages model, a reusable page-builder (text, media, headline, CTA, contact form sections) rendered by self-fetching Server Components, Portable Text rich text, a media pipeline covering responsive Sanity images, Mux video, Lottie and Rive, plus draft mode with Presentation tool and Visual Editing, SEO helpers, JSON-LD, and CMS-driven sitemaps. Its standout is agent-readiness: every page serves a token-light Markdown version to agents via Accept: text/markdown content negotiation, ships an editable llms.txt drafted from your content, a published openapi.json, real 404s that return a Markdown recovery map instead of an error string, and AGENTS.md plus scoped skills with two preconfigured MCP servers (one reading the dev server, one driving real Chrome for screenshots and performance traces). Extras include Next.js Cache Components with webhook-only revalidation, optional HTTP basic auth, RSS, CMS-managed redirects, Umami analytics, spam prevention, Plop scaffolding, a seed dataset, and npm run trim to strip unneeded features cleanly. One commercial license per buyer covers unlimited personal, commercial, and client projects.
